primary_work.title: Isolated Causal Effects of Natural Language

decision: NARROWED BEYOND ISOLATED CAUSAL EFFECTS OF PREDEFINED LANGUAGE INTERVENTIONS — NOT ADOPTED
prior_art_boundary: causal effects of predefined language attributes on external outcomes are prior art
isolating a focal language effect by transporting non-focal language to a common target distribution is prior art
doubly robust language-effect estimation and omitted-variable-bias sensitivity analysis are prior art
fidelity and overlap metrics for non-focal language representations are prior art
a reproducible external causal effect of a supplied language attribute does not imply discovery of raw-language equivalence, latent intervention targets, or denotation
assumptions: no unmeasured confounding conditional on non-focal language
specified target distribution over non-focal language
correct propensity or outcome nuisance model for doubly robust identification
counterexample: Two models can share the complete observed text distribution, supplied focal codebook, propensity score, outcome regression, IATE and IATT isolated effects, doubly robust estimating equation, fidelity and overlap metrics, omitted-variable-bias bounds, external outcomes, action accuracy, and task success while one treats two utterance forms as synonyms denoting one latent target and the other treats them as distinct classes denoting observationally aliased latent targets. A simultaneous focal-label, potential-outcome-index, and sign-convention recoding also preserves the observed law. Therefore isolated language effects identify a causal contrast relative to a predefined codebook, not the raw-language equivalence relation, latent intervention-target partition, or their denotation.
official_code_status: paper-specific official code verified and exact commit pinned; aggregate Amazon and tirzepatide experiment scripts are documented; README does not establish immutable Python/dependency, dataset checksum, seed, raw-result, model-size, RSS, or wall-time manifests
